BiblicalUsage: Dagon was the god of the Philistines, and his story in Scripture is a story of falling down. The ark of the Lord was set beside him in his own temple, and by morning he lay face down before it, his head and hands broken off on the threshold. The Philistines also feasted before Dagon when they thought their god had delivered Samson into their hands, and Saul's armour was later hung in Dagon's house after his death on the battlefield.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe Dagon shows what every false god does in the end: it falls before the true God, and it cannot save the people who trust in it. My position is plain — there is one God, and idols are only wood and stone that break.
